punchline: The same brain performs very differently at nine in the morning and three in the afternoon.
thirty_sec: In When, Daniel Pink explains that most people's days follow a peak, trough and recovery. Larks and 'third birds' peak in the morning; owls often run in reverse. Analytic tasks go best at your peak, insight tasks can go better in the recovery, and routine work suits the trough. Danish students even scored lower on tests taken later in the day. His advice: match the task to the time.
question: Are you a lark, an owl or a third bird, and does your schedule reflect it?
